title: 'attempt to index nil'
summary: The most common runtime error: you wrote a.b.c but somewhere in the chain a value was nil. FindFirstChild returns nil instead of erroring — so chains silently break. Guard each hop.

explanation.whatItIs: Dot-walking into emptiness: one link of the path is nil, and indexing nil explodes with this message.
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox lookups are forgiving (FindFirstChild → nil) so MISSING isn't fatal — but USING the nil is.
symptoms: 'attempt to index nil with 'Position'' (or any member name)
Code that works in Studio, fails on live servers (replication timing!)
Works the second time — first run raced the object's creation
explanation.fix: Guard hops (local x = parent:FindFirstChild("X") if x then…), WaitForChild for async arrivals, assert() with a message during development.
tips: Read the error's MEMBER name — it tells you which hop was nil
Add timeouts to WaitForChild to avoid infinite yields
And-then chains: local a = b and b:FindFirstChild("c")
commonMistakes: Dot-indexing names that might not exist yet
Caching nil at startup and using it forever
Blaming 'Roblox' instead of the missing hop

examples.title: Guarded traversal
examples.code:
-- ❌ Explodes if Map or Spawn is missing:
-- local p = workspace.Map.Spawn.Position

-- ✅ Guard each hop:
local map = workspace:FindFirstChild("Map")
local spawn = map and map:FindFirstChild("Spawn")
if spawn then
    print("Spawn at", spawn.Position)
else
    warn("Map.Spawn missing — check hierarchy")
end

-- ✅ Async arrival:
local ok, part = pcall(function()
    return workspace:WaitForChild("Map", 5):WaitForChild("Spawn", 5)
end)
if not ok then warn("Spawn never appeared") end
